items.prompt: Which prefix makes the opposite of happy?

options.why: Dis- fits words like obey and agree, but dishappy is not a word.
Re- means again. Rehappy is not a word.
Pre- means before. Prehappy is not a word.

hints: Think of a word that means not happy.
Try each prefix in front of happy and say it aloud.
Start with the first one: dis + happy. Is dishappy a word you know?
items.explanation: Un- means not. Unhappy means not happy, so it is the opposite of happy.

items.prompt: The prefix re- means again. What does rewrite mean?

options.why: That would need a prefix that means not. Re- means again.
Before is the meaning of pre-, not re-.
Re- does not tell us anything about speed.

hints: Look at the two parts of the word: re and write.
Put the meaning of re- together with the word write.
Cover re- with your finger. What word is left? Now add the meaning of re-.
items.explanation: Re- means again, so rewrite means to write something again.

items.prompt:
Use un- or dis- to make the opposite of agree.
Lina and Joe ___ about which game to play.
hints: You need a word that means do not agree.
Try un- and dis- in front of agree. Which one is a real word?
Say unagree aloud. Does it sound right? Now try the other prefix.
items.explanation: Dis- means not. Disagree means not agree, so Lina and Joe want different games.

items.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
hints: Find the prefix at the start of each word.
Un- and dis- mean not. Re- means again.
Start with refill. Which meaning has the word again in it and is about filling?
items.explanation: Un- and dis- mean not, and re- means again. So unsafe is not safe, and refill is fill again.

items.prompt: Sort the words. Which prefix makes a real word?
hints: Say each word with a prefix in front, out loud.
Un- and dis- both mean not. Listen for the one that sounds like a real word.
Start with build. Which is a real word: unbuild, disbuild or rebuild?
items.explanation: We say unlucky, unfair and untidy; dishonest, disobey and disagree; rebuild, reheat and repaint.

items.prompt: The milk was left in the hot sun all day. Now it is ___ to drink.

options.why: Safely tells how you do something. The sentence needs a word that means not safe.
Resafe is not a word.
Dissafe is not a word. Safe takes a different prefix.

hints: Would you drink milk that sat in the hot sun all day?
You need a word that means not safe.
Try un-, dis- and re- in front of safe. Which sounds right?
items.explanation: Unsafe means not safe. Milk left in the hot sun can make you ill, so it is unsafe to drink.

items.prompt: Choose all the words where re- means again.

options.why: Here re is just part of the word. Dy is not a word.
Real is one whole word. Al again does not make sense.
Red is a colour. The letters re are just part of it.

hints: Cover re at the start. Is the rest a real word?
If the rest is a word, check that again makes sense with it.
Try replay: cover re and you see play. Does replay mean play again?
items.explanation: Replay, refill and reread mean play again, fill again and read again. In ready, real and red, the letters re are just part of the word.

items.prompt:
Add un-, dis- or re- to tie.
Ravi wants to take off his shoes, so first he has to ___ his laces.
hints: Think about what you do to laces before you take off your shoes.
You need a word that means the opposite of tie.
Which prefix means not or the opposite: un-, dis- or re-? Try each one with tie.
items.explanation: Untie means undo a knot. Ravi has to untie his laces before he can take off his shoes.

items.prompt: Which word does NOT have a prefix?

options.why: Unwell is un + well. It has the prefix un-.
Disobey is dis + obey. It has the prefix dis-.
Reuse is re + use. It has the prefix re-.

hints: A prefix is added to the front of a whole word.
Cover the first two or three letters. Is the rest a real word?
Try it with unwell: cover un and you see well, a real word. Now test the others.
items.explanation: In under, the letters un are just part of the word, because der is not a word. The others are a prefix plus a real word.

items.prompt: The magician waved his hand and the coin ___. Nobody could see it.

options.why: Reappeared means it came back again. But nobody could see the coin.
Unappeared is not a word.
Appeared means it came into view. That is the opposite of what happened.

hints: Read the second sentence. Can anyone see the coin?
You need a word that means stopped being seen.
Which prefix makes the opposite of appear?
items.explanation: Disappeared means went out of sight. Dis- turns appear into its opposite, and nobody could see the coin.

items.prompt: Kadek reused the jar for her pencils. What did Kadek do?

options.text: She did not use the jar.
options.why: That would be unused. Re- means again.
Nothing in the sentence says the jar broke.
Before is the meaning of pre-. Re- means again.

hints: Find the prefix in reused.
What does the prefix re- mean?
Cover re. The word left is used. Now add the meaning of re-.
items.explanation: Re- means again, so reused means used again. Kadek used the jar again to hold her pencils.

items.prompt:
One word has the wrong prefix. Which one?
Bayu felt unwell and unhappy. His puppy was unobedient, and his room was untidy.

options.why: Unwell is correct. It means not well.
Unhappy is correct. It means not happy.
Untidy is correct. It means not tidy.

hints: Read each un- word and check that it sounds like a real word.
Obedient is in the same family as obey.
Start with unwell. Does diswell sound right? Try the same test on each word.
items.explanation: The right word is disobedient, not unobedient. Obedient takes dis-, just like obey.

hints: The word has seven letters.
It starts with the prefix un-.
Add un- to the word happy.
items.explanation: The word is unhappy. The prefix un- means not, so unhappy means not happy.
